Dark and light /l/
The /l/ sound can be pronounced in two ways
called ‘light’ and ‘dark’ /l/.
• We use the light /l/ before a vowel or
diphthong, e.g. London, light, flag, unless,
lovely.
• We use the dark /l/ as the final sound of
a syllable, after a vowel or diphthong, e.g.
full, able, will, April.
Some people confuse the /r/ and the /l/
sounds. When making the /r/ sound the
tongue does not touch the roof of the mouth,
whereas to make the /l/ sound it does.
